title: Surface tension is probably the paramount force determining cell form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Surface tension is probably the paramount force determining cell form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Of the physical forces that determine the forms of cells, solitary or in contact, surface tension is of great and probably paramount importance, usually acting together with gravity, mechanical pressure and osmosis.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Among the forces which determine the forms of cells, whether they be solitary or arranged in contact with one another, this force of surface-tension is certainly of great, and is probably of paramount importance.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Surface tension and the forms of cells”. Scope: all cells, solitary or in aggregates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Relative force contributions can be estimated in defined systems, but the global ranking is vague and all-cell scope is too broad. Existing data resolve selected cell types and perturbations, not the general claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit force-balance models to cell shapes using measured cortical or interfacial tension, gravity, pressure, osmosis, adhesion, and wall mechanics, then compare each factor's predictive contribution across representative cell types. Surface tension is paramount only if removing it causes the largest general loss of predictive accuracy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Walled and wall-less cells require different models.

Most datasets do not measure all competing forces.

'Paramount' needs an imposed quantitative criterion.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A force ranking is measurable in principle with aspiration, pressure and osmotic series, and such series exist for a small set of cell types in papers. They are not assembled, and they do not span solitary and aggregated cells at the stated scope. Shape archives alone cannot rank the forces, so the open data support only a proxy comparison.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For solitary cells and cells in contact, rank the contribution of surface tension against gravity, mechanical pressure and osmosis in predicting outline. Surface tension as the largest term across cell types would support the claim; pressure or cortical contractility dominating the shape residual would refute 'paramount'.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Joint measurements of tension, pressure and osmosis are scattered and cover few cell types.

'Paramount' needs an agreed decomposition of shape variance.

The wording already says 'probably', which softens a miss.
